### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4804794ade7011da75d246cb5d4ae802fd46394` — the merge of head `566d19b85869c8a444873f701b06c629d86fd5f0` into base `150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4804794ade7011da75d246cb5d4ae802fd46394 && git checkout d4804794ade7011da75d246cb5d4ae802fd46394
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9 566d19b85869c8a444873f701b06c629d86fd5f0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9 && git merge --no-ff 566d19b85869c8a444873f701b06c629d86fd5f0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b091cd85161182e2a0871713861d695717c7aeec`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23015 (body and all five comments: triage 6122995432, ruling A 6134056653, claim 6138406113, dev report 6141744005, ACCEPT 6141797380); the cross-lane declaration 6138419895 on #20966; ADR-0048's 2026-10-08 addendum with N.1 to N.4 as it stands on `main`; PR #23206's body, its 25-path file list and the net diff against `main` (merge base `8323cad97`, +1648 / -16); the check-runs on the head. The pinned sibling was read at `.objectui-sha` `088e0f705`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set narrowings the diff makes** (each RIGHT, each judged with the one reading):
- `defineStack`, and so `os validate`, `os build` and a source boot: two `isDefault: true` record pages for one object inside `pages` refuse `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` 422, one finding per object naming every page with its position. `collectDuplicateDefaultRecordPageErrors` sits beside the duplicate-entry check, ahead of the object-count early return, so a platform object's pages count. `composeStacks` refuses the pair across its inputs in the same envelope; under `manifest: 'preserve'` entries are keyed `holder|name`, so one name in two stacks is two pages. A name repeated inside one stack is the duplicate-entry finding only, not counted here a second time. RIGHT.
- `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` and `registerItem('page', item, 'name', packageId)`: `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` 422 with `object`, `incoming`, `existing` and every conflict in `conflicts`. RIGHT.
- `saveMetaItem` (so `PUT /api/v1/meta/page/:name`) and the draft promotion: the same code and status. RIGHT.

**One reading, and it matches `PageSchema` exactly.** `defaultRecordPageObject` reads `isDefault === true` (the key is `z.boolean().default(false)`); `type` absent or `'record'`, the absent case filled from `PAGE_TYPE_DEFAULT`, the same constant `PageSchema.type`'s `.default()` is now built from, so the schema's default and the reading cannot part; and `object` a non-empty string (`PageSchema.object` is an optional string; an empty one binds no object, so treating it as unbound lets nothing through). Every door calls this function: `stack.zod.ts`, `declaredDefaultRecordPages` and the item seam in objectql, `defaultRecordPageSaveRefusal` in metadata-protocol. RIGHT.

**No precedence ladder, no registration-order rule, no silent downgrade.** Whichever side arrives second is refused, in either order (pinned); `collisionPolicy: 'warn'` does not soften it (pinned); the renderer is left nothing to tie-break. RIGHT.

**The registry door's holder bookkeeping**, read against `registerItem`'s key derivation at the head:
- A composite slot is stored under `PACKAGE:NAME`, and `applyProtection(item, { packageId })` stamps `_packageId` with that same id, so a composite slot and the install claim of one package's page collapse to one holder key (`package:ID:page`), while two packages' pages under one name are two composite keys and two holders. Package ids are dotted and page names snake_case, so splitting a key at its last colon is exact. RIGHT.
- The bare slot (a `sys_metadata` hydration or a write-through, registered with no package id) shadows every composite slot and claim of its name, as every ADR-0005 read does; a bare slot carrying a real package stamp (the protocol grafts a row's `package_id` onto an overlay body as `_packageId`) is named as that package's page; the `'sys_metadata'` sentinel and `_provenance: 'org'` are excluded from "packaged". The demote-by-overlay case is pinned: the holders become empty. RIGHT.
- Same package again: `otherDefaultRecordPageHolders` drops the package's own holders and the bare slot of the very page being registered; a re-install REPLACES the package's claims; a reload and an upgrade that moves the default to another of its pages are pinned. RIGHT. One edge, pre-existing and not this diff's: `installPackage` does not evict a package's earlier items (ADR-0048 §3.4 overwrite semantics), so a default page a package DROPS in an upgrade stays as that package's residue in the item store and still counts as a holder for every other party until a restart. That errs loud, never silent.
- Mid-install refusal: `refuseDefaultRecordPageConflicts` sits after the namespace gate, the co-owned-object check and the security-catalog refusal and before `const now` and every mutation, and `declaredDefaultRecordPages` reads exactly the sources the engine's collection loop registers (`pages` and `plugins[].pages`, arrays only, one level; `registerPlugin` does not recurse), so a manifest's conflict is caught at the package door and never first at the item seam after a partial install. The test pins no package record and no page after a refusal. RIGHT.
- The item seam runs before `applyProtection` and the store, after the security seam. RIGHT.

**The save door.** Judged after the schema fold and `withDeclaredPageTypeDefault`, before the authoring gate and every write (`repo.put` is the method's last act; the awaits ahead of it read the lock, the existing item and the container collision, or fold the body in memory), in draft and in publish mode (the mode is derived above it, and the draft-then-publish case is pinned), and judged again in `promoteDraftForPublish` on `draftForGate` before `repo.promoteDraft`, which both `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts` run. The holders are the environment-wide active rows (`readActiveOverlayRows`, ADR-0131 D6) plus `SchemaRegistry.defaultRecordPageHoldersOf(object)` for every name no stored row holds; an environment-scoped protocol (no write-through) still reads `this.engine.registry`, so the shipped holders are seen, pinned on both topologies. An unprovisioned store reads as no rows; any other read failure propagates. The remedy text never prescribes overlaying a packaged page by name, which `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` would refuse. RIGHT.

**No value a real producer writes today is refused.** Measured at the head: seven objects, each with exactly one default record page. `sys_organization_detail` and `sys_user_detail` are authored in `@objectstack/platform-objects/pages` and registered once, by `plugin-auth`'s manifest; `sys_position_detail` the same, registered once by `plugin-security`; `sys_approval_request_detail` by `plugin-approvals`; `showcase_project_detail`, `showcase_task_detail` and `showcase_settings` by `examples/app-showcase`, where no other `isDefault: true` page binds those objects. `showcase_capability_map` is `type: 'home'`, outside the rule. `app-crm` and `app-todo` ship no `isDefault: true` record page. objectui at the pin `088e0f705`: `usePageAssignment` selects by `type === 'record'`, `object` and declaration order and never reads `isDefault`; nothing there produces a record page. The old row in `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` stated the retired "for its type" rule and is corrected. The green `Dogfood Regression Gate` on the head corroborates the showcase boot. RIGHT. The cloud pair is the ruling's own carried case, routed in ③.

**Public-surface additions the diff makes** (named here; their declaration is judged in ②): `defaultRecordPageObject` on `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` each +1, regenerated); `PageSchema.isDefault`'s `.describe()` (reference docs +1 row, no accept-set change); `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` under `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (regenerated `contract.mdx` and `error-code-ledger.mdx`); `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT_CODE` and the public method `SchemaRegistry.defaultRecordPageHoldersOf`, whose return type makes `DefaultRecordPageHolder` reachable, on `@objectstack/objectql`'s root entry. `DefaultRecordPageConflictError` is NOT exported from the barrel, which keeps every refusal class unexported by design, so the ACCEPT's "and their types" holds only through the method's return type. All RIGHT as surface. `PAGE_TYPE_DEFAULT` is read by `page.zod.ts` and not re-exported, which is fine.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: RIGHT.** `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `minor` with the `!` summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner and the ADR-0087 marker `registered page-default-record-page-one-per-object-refused`; `@objectstack/platform-objects` at `patch` for the four help-text leaves. A narrowing is breaking, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention; the body carries the FROM → TO table per door and the one-line fix. The D3 entry `18.page-default-record-page-one-per-object-refused` names the surface, the replacement, the reason and acceptance criteria, with no D2 conversion (which page stays the default is the author's fact) and no `relevantWhen`; both RIGHT.
- **The gate's reading.** `check-adr-0087-registration` reads breaking-ness from four signals, and signal (4) is the ARM alone, through `readClause2Line`: `narrowing` is the breaking signal; the value is not read there. The gate is green with either `no (narrowing)` or `yes (narrowing)`, and `yes (narrowing)` is a legal, self-tested shape ("a diff that widens one surface and narrows another").
- **The question the ACCEPT handed over, answered from the rule text.** The value answers one question, 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」; the public surface is what the built entry reaches, 「公开面 = 包构建后的入口声明所达,⛔ 不只数入口的再导出清单」, re-exported names plus every type reachable through their props, parameters and return types; and for a new error code the rule is explicit: 「错误码已发布面 = `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER`/`StandardErrorCode`:新码恒 `yes`,无门亦然,漏登即缺口」. This diff adds a new ledger code, a new `@objectstack/spec/ui` export, and a new objectql export plus a public method. **The right line is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.** `no (narrowing)` is what the claim, the PR body and the changeset body carry, and the landing rules name that case: 「错误的 `no` 是可审计的假申报」. The level needs no change (`yes` takes at least `minor`), the arm and the marker need no change, and the ADR-0087 gate's verdict does not move.
- **FAIL item.** Correct the line to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the changeset body and in the PR body. The claim's line is the dispatching seat's to correct in its own act; the path limb already hits, so the queue gate owes a contract review either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Census (dev flag):** answered RIGHT in ①. One wording note: the three platform pages are authored in `platform-objects` and registered by the two plugins; the registering package is the unit the rule counts, so the body's producer column names the right unit.
- **The cold-boot open question, judged as the ACCEPT asked.** Does ruling A's "refused at registration and at save" already reach `sys_metadata` hydration at a cold boot? **No.** The ruling names two doors and mirrors them on ADR-0048's 2026-10-08 addendum, whose N.3 keeps "a write with no package provenance, which is how every `sys_metadata` hydration arrives" outside the registration refusal, and whose cold-boot check exists only through a separate amendment with its own ruling record (6063176077 on #22307); the ruling's workload column names the schema rule, the registration refusal and the `os validate` refusal and no boot gate, and the claim's file surface matched that. The PR delivers both named doors and the stack door, states the boundary in the objectql module doc, the acceptance notes and the D3 acceptance criteria, and keeps the spec's claim as narrow as its enforcement (the TSDoc lists the doors). So this is a maintainer choice, correctly escalated under `open_questions`, not a FAIL item. Two facts the report understates, for that decision: the surviving pair forms only through the upgrade-then-restart sequence, but it then makes a hot install and a cold boot answer differently for the same composition, an order-dependence of the kind ruling A rejected in D; and AGENTS.md's startup-registry rule applies in the mirror sense (the package door concludes "no other holder" from a registry whose stored pages have not hydrated, and records the install). Option B therefore has a precedent-shaped home, the N.3 amendment pattern, if the maintainer wants it; it needs its own card and ruling, as the security catalog's did.
- **Rider `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`:** a prose face (not `references/`, not `releases/`), one row that restated the retired rule, no new page so no `meta.json` edit. Accepted.
- **Rider, the four `platform-objects` translation leaves:** the `en` leaf is hand-edited to the exact `page.form.ts` string, which is what the generator rewrites it to (`check:i18n` inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`); the `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` values are hand-written as the guardrail allows; structure unchanged, one line each. Accepted.
- **Out of scope, the cloud leg:** the ruling itself orders it (the cloud seat, before the engine bump). The measured fact that an environment save under a packaged page's name is refused `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` 403 (`page` has `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`) narrows the ruling's "overlay by name" remedy to environment-authored pages; the PR's refusal texts, TSDoc and D3 entry prescribe only `isDefault: false` or host composition for a packaged page, consistent with that fact. Routed under the fork clause to the cloud seat. RIGHT.
- **Out of scope, objectui#12195:** the spec now states the rule; the renderer leg is that card's. RIGHT.
- **Governed surfaces:** none of the 25 paths is governed (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). 1,664 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold. Same-repository head, not a fork.
- **Check-runs on the head**, read 2026-10-13T09:00Z: 30 success, 5 skipped (Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood matrix shard, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, all path-filtered or opt-in), 5 in progress (Test Core shards 1 to 5), 0 failure. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the Type Check jobs and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success. Not waited on.
